newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Foreign selling depresses Manila shares at close.
newsitem.headline: Foreign selling depresses Manila shares at close.

text.p: Heavy foreign selling hit Manila's index-linked shares, particularly property counters, which weighed down the main index by 1.17 percent at close.
The key index shed 33.96 points to close at 2,872.37 points amid a modest turnover.
"Foreign houses are generally on the sell side. Heavy foreign selling is very evident today," Wilfred Son Keng Po, chief operating officer of Angping Securities, said.
Leading the losers were Empire East Land Holdings Inc and its parent Megaworld Properties & Holdings Inc.
However, the two issues cut some of their losses by midsession after Empire officials said they were going to buy back some shares from the market.
Pilipino Telephone Corp was also sold down due to its poor first quarter earnings.
Kenneth Nerecina, research head of Vickers Ballas Securities (Phils) Inc, said first quarter earnings would steer the direction of most index heavyweights next week.
But many brokers expected the market to weaken further next week since they did not expect corporate first quarter results to provide big growth.
